answer: A juniper identity stands in a hollow clearing; each ring in its trunk is one verified epoch. To stop clones, every identity must compose its own sonnet: a bond of 30 POA locked for 15 epochs and slashed if any attestation is proven fake. A rotating set of auditor nodes samples 10% of bonds each epoch. An attacker running N fakes must keep all N bonds alive for the full 15-epoch vesting window while facing rising odds of a slash. Cost grows linearly with N plus a compounding audit term, so bulk cloning becomes uneconomic.
